candidates.title: Agentic World Action Models
candidates.title_zh: 智能体世界动作模型
candidates.abstract: Recent world action models provide visual foresight and future prediction for robot manipulation, but lack explicit mechanisms for compositional skill reuse. Agentic robotics combines code-based planning and reasoning with reusable skills, but often lacks predictive grounding in physical dynamics. We introduce AW-0, an agentic world action model framework that integrates code-based planning with joint video and action prediction. We jointly model code, future video, and robot actions as three coupled generative streams within a unified mixture-of-transformers architecture. Within this architecture a code expert generates parameterized skill routines and control logic while video and action experts generate future visual states and low-level motor commands. Code serves two complementary roles: it structures multi-step prediction and control within the world model and represents skills as reusable programs for subsequent agentic execution. We further introduce an automated curation pipeline that labels robot and human video trajectories with aligned programs and consolidates recurring routines into reusable skill libraries. Evaluations on RoboTwin 2.0 and physical bimanual manipulation tasks show improved task performance over VLA and WAM baselines, alongside gains in language following, semantic reasoning and robustness, demonstrating that agentic code enables connection between planning, prediction and execution within WAMs.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出AW-0框架，用统一混合Transformer联合生成代码、未来视频与机器人动作，将技能表示为可复用程序，并在RoboTwin 2.0和双臂操作任务上超越VLA与世界动作模型基线。
candidates.contribution_zh: 将代码规划、视频预测和底层动作耦合为三条生成流，构建可复用技能库，实现规划、预测与执行的贯通。

ai_review.reason: 机器人世界动作模型，联合视频动作预测与代码规划，直接服务具身操作

candidates.title: Rethinking Video Autoencoders for Interactive World Models
candidates.title_zh: 重新思考用于交互式世界模型的视频自编码器
candidates.abstract: Video world models predict future frames from past frames and actions. They serve as simulators in which agents train, plan or are evaluated, and that humans can control interactively. They generate in the latent space of a video autoencoder, whose compression sets their cost per frame and how long each action waits to take effect. Yet world models often reuse the autoencoders of text-to-video generators, built for offline generation with no agent waiting and, without their training data and code, not retrainable at another compression. We therefore ask how, where and how much a world model should compress. We build CADRE, an open family of causal diffusion representation autoencoders spanning multiple spatio-temporal compressions. Its members differ only in a small bottleneck on frozen features and share a diffusion decoder self-distilled to one or a few steps. We train the same world model on each autoencoder in two domains, manipulation and navigation, with two environments each. CADRE forms most of the latency-quality frontier, especially with a moving camera. Our study also leads to four findings. At strong compression, a diffusion decoder is sharper than perceptual regression. In robot manipulation, temporal compression is more effective in the autoencoder than in the world model. Manipulation and navigation call for opposite compressions: temporal compression costs little when the camera is still, and spatial compression when it moves. Surprisingly, with a still camera, coarser spatial tokens hurt motion far more than image quality. Code, models and a live demo are at https://kyutai.org/blog/2026-10-21-cadre
candidates.summary_zh: 研究交互式视频世界模型应如何压缩潜空间，构建CADRE因果扩散表示自编码器族，在不同时空压缩下训练同一世界模型，并在操作与导航任务中评估延迟-质量权衡。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出可开源复现的CADRE自编码器族，系统分析时空压缩对交互式世界模型延迟、画质与运动保真度的影响，并给出操作/导航的四点发现。

ai_review.reason: 直接研究交互式视频世界模型的潜空间压缩，并在机器人操作与导航中评估，属具身世界模型核心范围。

candidates.title: PhysiCalWorld: In-Context Physics Calibration for World Models
candidates.title_zh: PhysiCalWorld：面向世界模型的情境内物理校准
candidates.abstract: Existing world models typically perceive a scene through current visual frame or a narrow history window. However, these observations may not reveal the physics properties that determine transition dynamics, such as an object's mass distribution, joint damping, or surface friction. Without calibrating these physics factors for world models, predictions tend to regress toward an empirical prior and induce severe drift in novel test scenes. To this end, we propose PhysiCalWorld, which calibrates action-conditioned world models to the instance-specific dynamics via in-context prompting, without fine-tuning or analytical physics modeling. Our method encodes an exploratory interaction clip collected within the test scene into a compact physics descriptor token, which grounds subsequent predictions in the scene's actual physical behavior. PhysiCalWorld is trained end-to-end with the latent prediction loss alone, without physics labels. At inference time, the descriptor token is extracted once and can be reused across rollouts with negligible compute overhead. We evaluate PhysiCalWorld across four environments covering diverse physics variations and show that it substantially improves rollout prediction accuracy and visual planning success rate. The learned descriptors also form a physically structured latent space and generalize beyond the physics ranges seen during training.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出用测试场景内一段探索交互片段编码成紧凑的物理描述子 token，以情境提示方式把动作条件世界模型校准到该实例的动力学，无需微调或解析建模，显著提升推演精度与视觉规划成功率。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出免微调的情境内物理校准机制：单次提取可复用的物理描述子 token，仅用潜预测损失端到端训练，形成结构化物理潜空间并具跨范围泛化。

ai_review.reason: 面向动作条件世界模型的物理参数在上下文校准，直接服务机器人预测与规划。

candidates.title: ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models
candidates.title_zh: ALPS：面向世界模型的视觉状态编码器
candidates.abstract: World models turn visual representations into predictions and actions. We argue that their visual foundation should combine physical-state information, native language alignment, and pixel reconstruction, so that a single representation can support prediction, instruction, and inspection. However, existing encoders typically specialize in only one or two of these capabilities; we therefore introduce ALPS, a pretrained visual state encoder that unifies all three in a single set of patch tokens. Using only still images and text, we pretrain a ViT-B/16 from scratch with language, reconstruction, and spatial correspondence objectives, and then refine it via cross-view self-distillation. In a unified evaluation across fifteen public encoders, ALPS achieves the lowest aggregate LIBERO state-probe error among ViT-B models (matching the 3.5x larger V-JEPA 2-L) while maintaining strong language alignment and accurate pixel reconstruction. Downstream, frozen ALPS tokens reach the highest mean policy success on LIBERO (85.5%) when paired with our native text tower, match or exceed leading encoders on world-model planning across PushT, Wall, and Granular, and allow predicted future tokens to be decoded directly into pixels for visual inspection. We hope this work helps establish visual pretraining as a shared foundation for understanding, prediction, and action in world models.
candidates.summary_zh: ALPS 从头预训练 ViT 视觉状态编码器，统一物理状态、语言对齐与像素重建，在 LIBERO 策略和 PushT 等世界模型规划任务中验证。
candidates.contribution_zh: 以语言、重建和跨视角自蒸馏联合预训练视觉状态编码器，提升机器人状态探测、策略成功率与可解码的世界模型规划。

provenance.source_comment: 35 pages (15 main + 20 supplementary), 13 figures, 26 tables. Project page: https://ucsc-vlaa.github.io/ALPS/ Code: https://github.com/UCSC-VLAA/ALPS

ai_review.reason: 提出面向世界模型的视觉状态编码器，直接服务机器人规划与策略，符合收录范围。

candidates.title: CW-WAM: A Structured Contact-Wrench World Action Model for Force-Sensitive Manipulation
candidates.title_zh: CW-WAM：用于力敏感操作的结构化接触力旋量世界动作模型
candidates.abstract: Force-sensitive manipulation requires contact and load information that is not provided explicitly by visual observations. We present CW-WAM, a world action model that jointly predicts video, motion, and contact wrench. Inspired by hybrid motion-force control, it contains a unified interaction module that treats both motion and contact wrench as modeling targets and predicts time-aligned motion-wrench chunks as control references. A pair-causal attention mechanism structures the motion-wrench dependencies, while a long fixed-length wrench memory retains past interaction information. The predicted wrench chunk acts as a force reference for a 20-Hz outer-loop admittance controller within a slow-fast control system that maintains force feedback and smooth motion between model queries. CW-WAM improves contact prediction and increases the insertion success rate from 25% to 70% for square pegs with 1-mm clearance per side and from 40% to 95% for power adapters, compared with WAM without wrench input. It also improves lifting-height accuracy across different loads. Our framework with an admittance controller reduces force-reference RMSE from 4.8 to 2.7 N for peg insertion and from 2.0 to 1.3 N for wiping, respectively, with smaller force fluctuations during successful execution. Project website: https://cw-wam-project.github.io/
candidates.summary_zh: 提出联合预测视频、运动与接触力旋量的世界动作模型，将预测力旋量作为导纳控制器的力参考，在插孔和擦拭任务中提升成功率与力跟踪精度。
candidates.contribution_zh: 统一建模运动与接触力旋量，设计配对因果注意力与力旋量记忆，并结合慢快导纳控制实现力敏感操作。

candidates.title: AtomicRL: Atomic Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
candidates.title_zh: AtomicRL：面向长时程机器人操作的原子强化学习
candidates.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown promise in robotic manipulation, but imitation learning (IL) alone often struggles to master complex long-horizon skills. Reinforcement learning (RL) offers an effective avenue for further improving VLA policies. However, existing VLA-RL methods typically suffer from delayed and biased credit assignment due to trajectory-level sparse rewards, while imbalanced subtask mastery creates bottlenecks that limit overall performance. To address these challenges, we propose AtomicRL, an RL post-training framework that leverages atomic task structures for reliable credit assignment and adaptive exploration. AtomicRL introduces Semantic-Aware Policy Optimization (SAPO), which uses semantic-aware gating to constrain TD residuals from failed atomic subtasks from propagating across task boundaries, mitigating credit contamination while preserving intra-subtask credit assignment and value bootstrapping. In addition, Bottleneck-Adaptive Target Exploration (BATE) dynamically coordinates task sampling and local exploration incentives based on the mastery of individual atomic subtasks, directing learning toward the remaining bottlenecks. Finally, we develop a Real2Sim2Real pipeline that bridges online RL in simulation with real-world deployment, facilitating practical transfer to physical robots. On LIBERO-LONG, AtomicRL achieves absolute performance gains of 3.6% and 4.0% over PPO across two VLA architectures. On CALVIN ABC-D, it improves full-task performance by up to 9.5% over PPO. Combined with the Real2Sim2Real pipeline, AtomicRL further improves real-world task performance by an average of 21.3%. These results demonstrate that AtomicRL effectively improves the learning efficiency and manipulation performance of VLA policies on long-horizon tasks.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出AtomicRL，对VLA策略进行强化学习后训练，利用原子任务结构改善信用分配与探索，并通过Real2Sim2Real迁移到真实机器人。
candidates.contribution_zh: 引入语义感知策略优化与瓶颈自适应探索，缓解长时程稀疏奖励信用污染，并构建仿真到真实迁移流程。

ai_review.reason: 聚焦VLA长时程机器人操作与强化学习后训练，属具身智能范围。

candidates.title: SP-HLM: Sparse-Pose-Driven Motion Generation and Whole-Body Control for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
candidates.title_zh: SP-HLM：稀疏位姿驱动的运动生成与全身控制用于人形机器人移动操作
candidates.abstract: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires an effective interface between high-level task policies and whole-body control. Existing interfaces typically rely on a single action representation for both task intent and whole-body coordination. This may burden the high-level policy or leave one aspect underspecified. We present SP-HLM, a framework built on a sparse-pose-driven interface. The interface combines five task-critical body poses with a learned latent motion prior to represent spatial intent and whole-body coordination in complementary forms. SP-VLA, a vision-language-action model, first predicts task-relevant sparse poses and finger joint positions from multimodal observations and language instructions using asynchronous action-chunk inference. Given these sparse targets, SP-MGM, a motion generation model trained through two-stage distillation, reconstructs coordinated full-body motion in real time. A pretrained motion encoder maps this motion to a compact latent representation. SP-GMT, a general motion tracker, then integrates the explicit sparse targets with this implicit motion prior for whole-body control. Experiments in simulation and on a real humanoid robot demonstrate improved motion tracking, whole-body coordination, and loco-manipulation success over existing approaches. Additional results and videos are available on our \href{https://sp-hlm.github.io/}{\textcolor{blue}{project page}}.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出以五个任务关键身体位姿加隐式运动先验构成的稀疏位姿接口，由VLA预测稀疏位姿与手指关节，运动生成模型实时重建全身动作，再经通用运动跟踪器实现人形移动操作控制。
candidates.contribution_zh: 设计稀疏位姿驱动的层次接口，解耦任务意图与全身协调；结合VLA、两阶段蒸馏运动生成与运动跟踪器，在仿真与真机上提升跟踪与移动操作成功率。

candidates.title: Looking Ahead: Modeling Future Evolution in Autoregressive Video Generation
candidates.title_zh: 前瞻：建模自回归视频生成中的未来演化
candidates.abstract: Autoregressive video diffusion models generate videos chunk by chunk, yet producing plausible continuations does not guarantee that they capture how scenes evolve. Under teacher forcing, strong temporal redundancy may allow local visual continuity to serve as a shortcut for current-chunk denoising, reducing the pressure to model visual evolution. We introduce Future Chunk Prediction (FCP), an auxiliary objective jointly optimized with teacher-forced denoising that predicts temporally separated chunks without access to the intervening visual context. Drawing supervision directly from training videos, FCP requires no additional pretrained visual encoder and leaves autoregressive inference unchanged. Our method achieves superior physical plausibility over standard teacher-forced autoregressive training with a lower overall training compute budget, highlighting the effectiveness and efficiency of future-chunk supervision for modeling visual evolution. Intriguingly, our visualizations suggest that FCP fosters a more structured representation space, which may be valuable for building autoregressive world models.
candidates.summary_zh: 针对自回归视频扩散模型依赖时间冗余、忽视场景演化的问题，提出未来块预测辅助目标，在无中间视觉上下文时预测间隔块，无需额外编码器且不改变推理。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出FCP辅助目标并与教师强制去噪联合优化，以更低训练算力提升物理合理性，并显示更结构化的表示空间，利于自回归世界模型。

ai_review.reason: 聚焦自回归视频生成的未来演化建模，提升物理合理性，可服务世界模型与生成式仿真。

candidates.title: CausalAlign: Causal Alignment of Video Generation Models for Consistent Ego-Motion
candidates.title_zh: CausalAlign：面向一致自运动的视频生成模型因果对齐
candidates.abstract: Diffusion-based video generation models (VGMs) can produce visually plausible videos, yet their camera ego-motion often drifts over long horizons. Camera ego-motion determines how the viewpoint changes between frames and is essential for maintaining consistent geometry and trajectories. To address this problem, we propose CausalAlign, a causal alignment framework with two components. First, we diagnose how precise ego motion is represented, used, and retained within VGMs using linear probes and causal interventions, revealing a rise-and-fall pattern during denoising. Second, we strengthen ego-motion state in VGM by aligning the representations at the identified layers to a 3D foundation model through delta-token space. This space encodes the changes between consecutive frames, allowing the alignment to focus on ego-motion dynamics rather than static scene content. With Wan2.2 fine-tuned on DL3DV and RealEstate10K, CausalAlign can largely improve motion accuracy, geometric consistency, and temporal smoothness, while preserving visual quality. For example, it improves geometric consistency by more than 20% relative to the base model. Moreover, with the fine-tuned VGM, CausalAlign improves the success rate of world action models (WAMs) by 10 points on mobile manipulation tasks of RoboCasa365 benchmark. Overall, CausalAlign improves ego-motion consistency in diffusion-based VGMs and yields noticeable gains in embodied models.
candidates.summary_zh: 论文诊断视频生成模型的自运动表示，并通过delta-token空间对齐3D基础模型，提升长时视频几何一致性与平滑性，并提高世界动作模型在RoboCasa365上的操作成功率。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出因果对齐框架，定位并强化视频生成模型中的自运动状态，以delta-token对齐3D基础模型，显著提升运动精度、几何一致性和具身模型性能。

ai_review.reason: 改进视频生成世界模拟器的自运动一致性，并在具身操作任务上验证，符合收录范围。

candidates.title: GeoMem-VLA: Internalizing 3D Scene Understanding into Temporal Memory for Vision-Language-Action Models
candidates.title_zh: GeoMem-VLA：将3D场景理解内化为视觉-语言-动作模型的时序记忆
candidates.abstract: Geometric structure is essential for robotic manipulation and understanding the 3D world. Most VLA models rely on 2D representations of current observations, while geometry-aware approaches often require additional 3D information. However, geometry inferred independently from individual observations is often discarded rather than accumulated into a persistent task representation. Our key insight is that action generation needs a compact, task-relevant geometric abstraction that can be continuously updated, rather than a complete, renderable 3D reconstruction at every step. We introduce GeoMem-VLA, a VLA framework that internalizes explicit 3D supervision into dedicated geometric tokens and maintains them as temporal memory for action generation, without directly aligning the VLM's native visual embeddings with the teacher feature space. During training, a frozen geometry foundation model supervises learnable GeoPlan tokens through a geometric flow-matching objective over the current scene point map and future end-effector tracks. These tokens are integrated with the memory of observation representations, where historical information is retrieved, adaptively fused with current observations, and consolidated to retain event frames as the task progresses. At inference, the policy retrieves historical representations and fuses them with the current working representation to predict actions, without invoking the 3D teacher or explicitly reconstructing the scene. After benchmark-specific downstream adaptation, GeoMem-VLA achieves 98.9% average success on LIBERO and 91.10% / 91.24% on RoboTwin's clean/randomized settings. Across five real-world tasks, GeoMem-VLA achieves 78.0% average success. These results suggest that internalizing and remembering 3D scene understanding is a promising approach to robot control.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出GeoMem-VLA，用几何流匹配将冻结3D基础模型的监督注入可学习GeoPlan令牌，并与历史观测记忆融合；推理无需3D教师或显式重建，在LIBERO、RoboTwin及真实任务上验证。
candidates.contribution_zh: 将显式3D监督内化为几何令牌与时序记忆，避免推理时3D重建，提升VLA操作成功率。

ai_review.reason: 面向机器人操作的VLA框架，内化3D几何并维护时序记忆，直接服务具身控制。

candidates.title: Robot Generalization Beyond Volume: The Diversity Path via Zero-Shot Capabilities
candidates.title_zh: 超越数据量的机器人泛化：通过零样本能力实现多样性路径
candidates.abstract: General-purpose robots must handle tasks, objects and environments they were never trained on, yet zero-shot generalization remains one of the least solved problems in physical AI. In digital AI, zero-shot capability grew with the volume and, above all, the diversity of training data, much of it sourced from the crowd. Robotics instead relies on paid collection by a few well-funded teams, which yields volume without diversity. We formulate zero-shot generalization in physical AI as coverage of the deployment distribution, and show that more samples from the same collectors shrink the unseen region only slowly, while each new contributor can extend it. Building on this and on zero-shot learning, we propose a shared latent space for robot actions that combines multi-modal alignment, generative augmentation, and noisy-label learning. As a scalable source of diverse data, we propose a community of developers building applications on one standard, approachable robot, Origami. We close with a testable hypothesis and an evaluation protocol relating real-robot zero-shot success to the diversity of contributed data.
candidates.summary_zh: 将物理AI零样本泛化视为部署分布覆盖问题，指出数据多样性比单一来源数据量更关键，并提出共享机器人动作潜空间与社区数据方案。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出以部署覆盖衡量零样本泛化，结合多模态对齐、生成增强和噪声标签学习构建共享动作潜空间，并给出社区数据假设与评测协议。

candidates.title: Post-hoc Epistemic Uncertainty for Vision-Language-Action Policies
candidates.title_zh: 视觉-语言-动作策略的事后认知不确定性
candidates.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies need to recognize gaps in their training knowledge to request useful demonstrations or assistance in new situations, especially when failures are costly. Disagreement within an ensemble of independently trained policies can guide these decisions, but requires training and running multiple policies. We propose post-hoc kernel-variance heads that estimate epistemic uncertainty from the embeddings of a single policy. Each head computes the conditional variance of a Gaussian process conditioned on embeddings from the training demonstrations. Fitting requires no regression targets or gradient updates and leaves the policy unchanged. In experiments with SmolVLA on LIBERO-10, the kernel variance heads perform competitively with two-policy ensemble scores in task-level correlation with task success, in demonstration acquisition during active learning, and in referral to a stronger supervisor policy as a proxy for human assistance. For SmolVLA, the head on the vision-language backbone reduces uncertainty-scoring time by up to approximately a factor of 50 compared with ensemble scores, while also substantially reducing setup costs. We also show that the established evaluation protocol on LIBERO-10 primarily rewards recognition of coverage differences between tasks, while execution variability weakens assessment of within-task rankings. Thus, controlled perturbations provide a complementary evaluation: modality-specific heads identify unfamiliar camera, instruction, or state inputs, while fused heads can detect unfamiliar combinations of individually familiar inputs. With a supervisor proxy trained on the evaluated perturbation families, the decoder head improves within-task referral over ensemble disagreement. These findings show that useful uncertainty estimates for adaptive robot learning can be obtained from a single policy.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出事后核方差头，从单一VLA策略嵌入估计认知不确定性，无需重训或多策略集成，并在LIBERO-10上验证主动学习、求助与扰动检测效果。
candidates.contribution_zh: 用高斯过程条件方差构建事后不确定性头，保持策略不变，以单策略接近集成效果并显著降低评分时间与部署成本。

ai_review.reason: 面向VLA策略的不确定性估计，直接服务机器人主动学习与求助。

candidates.title: FlowVLA: Learning Flow-Aware Physical Completion for Quantitative Robotic Pouring
candidates.title_zh: FlowVLA：学习流感知物理完成以实现定量机器人倾倒
candidates.abstract: During steady pouring, images and robot pose may remain nearly unchanged while transferred mass accumulates, making the return decision ambiguous for a whole-task vision-language-action (VLA) policy. We present FlowVLA, which separates motor generation from physical-completion estimation. A shared $π_{0.5}$ action expert learns approach, pour, and return with boundary-aware supervision. A target-independent estimator fuses visual, joint, wrist-wrench, and recurrent force-belief histories to maintain an estimate of transferred mass. The controller initiates return when this estimate plus predicted residual outflow reaches the requested mass. In coffee-pot/water experiments, FlowVLA achieves 13.1 g goal-balanced mean absolute error (MacroMAE), lower than all tested VLA baselines. Across all attempts, 53.7% both complete the task and finish within +/-10% of the requested mass. The same model interpolates to held-out 150/250-g targets without retraining. Independently trained models further evaluate the formulation in three additional container-fluid settings.
candidates.summary_zh: FlowVLA将动作生成与物理完成估计解耦，融合视觉、关节、腕部力/力矩及循环力信念历史估计转移质量，达到目标质量时触发返回，实现定量机器人倾倒。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出流感知VLA框架，将倾倒动作与质量完成判断分离，无需目标重训即可泛化到150/250克目标。

ai_review.reason: 机器人倾倒VLA，含力觉物理完成估计与闭环控制，属具身智能范围。

candidates.title: Toward Recursive Self-Improvement in Physical AI
candidates.title_zh: 迈向物理AI中的递归自我改进
candidates.abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) describes a system that improves not only its behavior but also the process by which it improves. Recent digital agents test this idea by rewriting their own code and checking each version with executable tests. Bringing these mechanisms into the physical world requires learning from partial observations through costly trials, while accounting for changing operating conditions and potentially irreversible consequences. We position RSI within robot learning and trace pathways from improving robot capabilities to improving the processes that generate them. We examine how physical experience can strengthen these improvement mechanisms and when the resulting gains can support further self-improvement of the mechanisms themselves. Gains carry forward only when feedback addresses remaining learning needs, the receiving component can use the change, its value survives changes in tasks or hardware, and continued practice remains safe and affordable. Existing studies, concentrated in manipulation, support behavioral improvement, benefits to later learning, and procedure improvement. Some systems also change the improver's knowledge or tools, but the physical studies reviewed here have yet to isolate gains attributable to recursion. We synthesize these findings into evaluation principles and research directions for machines that, trial by trial, safely improve the way they improve.

candidates.title: From VLM Planners to Robotic Agents: Self-Evolving Harnesses for History-Dependent Manipulation
candidates.title_zh: 从VLM规划器到机器人智能体：面向历史依赖操作的自进化执行框架
candidates.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models achieve strong performance across embodied manipulation tasks by unifying visual understanding, language conditioning, and action generation. However, long-horizon tasks can involve non-Markovian dependencies: successful decisions may require retaining task progress and past interaction outcomes, while partial observability and execution errors compound over time. Existing work has begun to address these challenges by augmenting foundation-model policies with memory and by introducing hierarchical architectures that separate high-level planning from low-level execution. We organize the high-level VLM as a robotic agent through an editable harness to maintain task context and improve planning through execution experience. We instantiate this approach as SERA (Self-Evolving Robotic Agent), with a fixed VLA executor providing low-level control. The harness maintains and updates task context using observations and execution feedback to guide subsequent planning. Self-evolution uses environment rollouts to propose and evaluate harness revisions, with the selected configuration fixed before held-out testing. On RoboMME, SERA achieves 51.38% overall success with autonomous selection, compared with 44.38% without self-evolution. Our exploration suggests that agentic planning is a promising direction for history-dependent robotic manipulation.
candidates.summary_zh: 将高层VLM组织为可编辑框架式机器人智能体，用观测与执行反馈维护任务上下文，并通过环境回放自进化框架配置，底层由固定VLA执行器控制；在RoboMME上提升长程操作成功率。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出SERA自进化机器人智能体框架，以可编辑harness承载历史上下文并借环境rollout迭代规划配置，验证智能体式规划对非马尔可夫操作任务有效。

ai_review.reason: 面向历史依赖的机器人长程操作，属VLA与具身智能规划范畴

candidates.title: Events, Not Pixels: Where World Models Get the Return Wrong
candidates.title_zh: 事件而非像素：世界模型回报错在哪
candidates.abstract: World models are increasingly used for planning, where a planner ranks candidate actions by returns imagined by the model. However, these models are judged mainly by how well they render frames, even though a visually faithful rollout can still assign the wrong return. To identify where this mismatch arises, we introduce a transition-level diagnostic that replaces imagined transitions with real ones and measures the reduction in return error against a budget-matched random control. Our analysis yields two findings. (1) Event transitions, the few steps where a reward is earned or an episode ends, are rendered as well as other steps (median pixel-error ratio 0.85), yet restoring them removes a median of 70% of the return error. In contrast, restoring transitions with the largest MSE, SSIM or LPIPS error removes less than a random choice. Across the 44 Atari-100k model--collection pairs that pass our reliability checks, including three released families, event patches outperform random patches in 39 (sign test p=1.4 x 10^{-7}), with a median gain of +44 percentage points. (2) The remaining error is structured: a complementary patch separates errors at true events from those elsewhere, while an eight-step timing tolerance recovers few events missed by our deterministic models. This structure also guides repair: a rule recorded before four repair outcomes were known predicts when a diffusion model repairs these failures. Event patches improve plan ranking, and the same concentration appears on control tasks with rare reward events.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出转移级诊断，用真实转移替换想象转移，发现事件转移虽渲染不差却承载大部分回报误差，修复事件可改善规划排序。
candidates.contribution_zh: 揭示世界模型回报误差集中于少数事件转移，而非像素误差最大处，并提供可指导修复与规划排序的诊断方法。

ai_review.reason: 面向世界模型规划与回报预测，属动作条件仿真与规划诊断，建议收录。

candidates.title: LiveAct: Towards Real-Time Multi-Agent World Models with Heterogeneous Action Interfaces
candidates.title_zh: LiveAct：迈向实时多智能体世界模型的异构动作接口
candidates.abstract: Interactive video world models predict how an environment evolves under user actions, but most existing systems assume one controlled agent and one task-specific action interface. We study multi-agent video world modeling, where one model generates a joint visual future for multiple controlled agents while interpreting heterogeneous controls ranging from binary game buttons to continuous robot commands. This task presents two complementary challenges. First, every agent-indexed action stream must control its intended visual entity independently. Second, the model must adapt the meaning of each control variable across different tasks, where the same tensor dimension may denote an attack, steering command, or robot command. We introduce LiveAct, centered on a Heterogeneous Action Interface (HAI) whose two components mirror this decomposition. To support independent control, Agent-Aware Spatial Modulation uses language-driven spatial gates and agent-specific attention to bind each action stream to its intended visual agent. To accommodate heterogeneous controls, Schema-Guided Action Adaptation describes each control variable in language and modulates its semantic token with the synchronized numerical value. We further transfer the complete interface to a blockwise causal generator through teacher forcing and rollout-aware distribution matching, enabling efficient streaming generation while retaining agent-specific control and action semantics. We instantiate the formulation on six multi-agent sources spanning games and multi-robot manipulation, and evaluate visual quality, action following, agent attribution, and latency. Across games and robot manipulation, LiveAct reaches 0.898 and 0.942 agent-attribution accuracy without agent locations or identity crops, and the causal generator attains 17.70 FPS at $512\times 448$.
candidates.summary_zh: 研究多智能体视频世界模型，用单一模型为多个受控智能体生成联合视觉未来，并同时解析从游戏按键到连续机器人指令的异构控制信号。提出异构动作接口，并通过教师强制与 rollout 感知分布匹配迁移到分块因果生成器，实现实时流式生成。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出智能体感知空间调制与模式引导动作适配，将每条动作流绑定到目标视觉实体并赋予跨任务语义；蒸馏为因果生成器后达 17.7 FPS，多智能体归属准确率 0.90 以上。

candidates.title: Plan First, Act Later: Streaming Reasoning for Executable Memory in Robot Control
candidates.title_zh: 先规划后执行：机器人控制中用于可执行记忆的流式推理
candidates.abstract: Long-horizon robot manipulation requires a robot to remember task-relevant information beyond its short observation window. Existing memory-augmented policies typically retrieve relevant information from history and reason over it at execution time, placing a heavy reasoning burden on the high-level model. To address this challenge, we propose PAL (\textbf{P}lan first, \textbf{A}ct \textbf{L}ater), a hierarchical memory framework for vision-language robot manipulation. It maintains a short-term visual buffer, a semantic-event memory, and an executable \texttt{subtask\_list}. A high-level vision-language model (VLM) converts streaming visual observations into the \texttt{subtask\_list}. At execution time, the VLM selects the currently relevant subtask from the \texttt{subtask\_list} and passes it to a low-level vision-language-action (VLA) policy. To teach the model what to write to memory and when to update it, we introduce a two-stage data generation procedure that first expands sparse update supervision and then uses self-labeling with task-grounded verification to generate training data that better match the state distribution encountered during execution. We evaluate our approach on memory-dependent benchmarks and real-world manipulation tasks. On RoboMME, PAL achieves a \textbf{56.05\%} success rate, outperforming the strongest baseline, FrameSamp-Modul, at 44.51\%. In real-world experiments across four manipulation tasks, \pal{} reaches \textbf{60.83\%} overall success, surpassing MemER (45.00\%) and FrameSamp-Modul (28.33\%). These results show that proactively writing future-relevant subtasks into hierarchical memory improves long-horizon visual reasoning and robot control. Code and videos can be found on our website: https://qinghangliu.github.io/pal-webpage/
candidates.summary_zh: 提出PAL分层记忆框架，用高层VLM将流式视觉观测转为可执行子任务列表，低层VLA选择执行；两阶段数据生成训练记忆写入与更新。在RoboMME和真实操作任务上提升长程操作成功率。
candidates.contribution_zh: 构建短期视觉缓冲、语义事件记忆与可执行子任务列表的分层记忆，并通过两阶段自标注数据生成降低执行时推理负担。

candidates.title: LLM-Based Exogenous World Modeling for Dynamic Scheduling
candidates.title_zh: 基于LLM的外生世界建模用于动态调度
candidates.abstract: Dynamic scheduling requires dispatching online arrivals while anticipating future jobs, as poor decisions can compound downstream costs under nonlinear tardiness objectives. We show that a pretrained large language model (LLM) can serve as the exogenous component of a structured world model, forecasting uncertain future job arrivals. Specifically, we exploit an afterstate decomposition, which separates known deterministic shop transitions from uncertain exogenous job arrivals, enabling the LLM to forecast only the latter through a compact belief representation. Building on this, we develop Afterstate World-Model Planning (AWMP), which combines an evolved, belief-conditioned dispatching strategy with short scenario-based rollouts. A surprise-triggered refresh mechanism queries the LLM only when newly observed arrivals deviate sufficiently from previous forecast, and online residual self-calibration further conditions the LLM on its recent forecast errors to handle nonstationary arrivals. Across diverse arrival distributions, AWMP reduces weighted tardiness by 6-21% on dynamic job-shop and 22-46% on flexible job-shop benchmarks, relative to the best of eight classical priority-dispatching rules.
candidates.summary_zh: 论文将预训练LLM作为结构化世界模型的外生模块，预测动态调度中不确定的任务到达，并提出AWMP规划方法，在作业车间基准上降低延迟成本。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出afterstate分解、惊喜触发刷新与在线残差校准，用LLM预测外生到达并结合短视滚动规划优化调度。

ai_review.reason: 面向作业车间动态调度，非机器人/具身智能，无物理交互或动作控制。

candidates.title: Relational Geometry Forcing for World Action Models
candidates.title_zh: 世界动作模型的关系几何强制
candidates.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) have shown strong potential for robot manipulation by jointly learning visual dynamics and executable actions. However, their video and action objectives do not explicitly constrain the 3D geometry that is crucial for precise manipulation. Recently, geometry-aware WAMs introduce depth or 4D prediction branches, whereas representation alignment methods supervise intermediate WAM features with pretrained 3D foundation models. Yet we find that such pointwise alignment benefits the video features but degrades action learning, since dense geometric feature targets overly restrict compact action features. To address this limitation, we propose Relational Geometry Forcing (RGF), which transfers geometric priors from a frozen 3D foundation model by aligning pairwise feature relations instead of pointwise features. Specifically, RGF applies three complementary relational objectives, where intra-frame and cross-view relations transfer scene geometry and multi-view correspondence to the video features, while action-temporal relations couple action dynamics to geometric scene evolution. Applied only during training, RGF requires no explicit geometry branch or extra inference module. Extensive experiments in simulation and the real world demonstrate the effectiveness of Relational Geometry Forcing, showing consistent gains across diverse manipulation scenarios and WAM paradigms.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出关系几何强制RGF，通过帧内、跨视角和动作时序的关系对齐，从冻结3D基础模型向世界动作模型迁移几何先验，无需额外几何分支或推理模块，在仿真和真实操作中提升精度。
candidates.contribution_zh: 将点式几何对齐改为成对关系对齐，避免过度约束动作特征，并以三类关系目标耦合动作动态与场景几何演化。

ai_review.reason: 面向机器人操作的世界动作模型，用关系几何对齐提升3D几何与动作学习，属具身智能范畴。

candidates.title: Training in Deployment: Human-in-the-loop Online Post-Training for Robot Manipulation
candidates.title_zh: 部署中训练：面向机器人操作的人在回路在线后训练
candidates.abstract: Large pretrained robot foundation models provide strong priors for manipulation, yet adapting them to target tasks with offline teleoperated demonstrations often fails to cover the contact-rich, recovery, and precision-critical states encountered during deployment. Existing methods mitigate this issue by augmenting offline demonstrations with human-in-the-loop data or online reinforcement learning. Despite this, offline post-training adapts slowly because it cannot immediately absorb deployment experience, while online RL typically relies on value functions or auxiliary actor-critic models, increasing both training complexity and instability. We present TIDE (Training In DEployment), a human-in-the-loop online post-training system. TIDE introduces a provenance-conditioned supervised learning framework that updates the policy online from human interventions and policy-generated rollouts collected during deployment, without a learned critic, reward model, or action scorer. Across four real-world bimanual manipulation tasks, TIDE improves milestone-normalized task progress and binary full-task completion over the warm-start policy and matched additional offline demonstrations, and performs comparably to the fixed-policy collection baseline while making updated checkpoints available during deployment. Each task-specific online post-training session, from the start of deployment rollouts until the final checkpoint is available, completes in less than one hour while learning and checkpoint handling run asynchronously.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出TIDE人在回路在线后训练系统，利用部署中的人类干预与策略 rollout 进行溯源条件监督学习，无需 critic、奖励模型或动作评分器，在四项真实双臂操作任务中快速提升任务进度与完成率。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出无需价值函数或奖励模型的溯源条件在线监督后训练框架，使机器人基础模型在部署中快速适应接触丰富与恢复任务。

ai_review.reason: 直接面向机器人操作策略的部署适应，属具身智能与机器人基础模型应用，证据充分。

candidates.title: Failure Modes of Vision-Language Models for Human Activity Understanding in Thermal HRI
candidates.title_zh: 热成像人机交互中视觉语言模型人类活动理解的失效模式
candidates.abstract: Thermal cameras enable robots to perceive human activities in darkness while revealing less personally identifiable appearance information and fewer details of the surrounding environment than RGB cameras. As vision-language models (VLMs), originally developed for RGB imagery, are increasingly integrated into embodied systems for scene understanding and high-level planning, thermal sensing offers a promising way to extend activity perception to low-light and privacy-sensitive settings. However, the failure modes of VLMs in thermal human activity understanding for human-robot interaction (HRI) remain underexplored. We fill this gap by evaluating seven locally deployable VLMs, including models developed for physical AI and robotics, on two person-centric thermal datasets. Our diagnostic tasks examine fine-grained action recognition, activity timeline reconstruction, and the ability to withhold unsupported answers. Paired RGB recordings serve as a performance reference, while controlled variations in frame sampling, thermal input presentation, and reasoning are used to assess whether the observed errors can be mitigated. Our results show that models can recognize broad activity categories but struggle with fine-grained actions such as coughing, sneezing, and yawning. They also produce inaccurate event timelines and hallucinate actions involving objects. Simple thermal input preprocessing and additional reasoning offer only limited, model-dependent gains. Abstention behavior also varies across models even under explicit instructions, limiting their reliability for practical robotic use.
candidates.summary_zh: 在两个人本热成像数据集上评测7个可本地部署的VLM（含机器人模型），诊断细粒度动作识别、活动时间线重建与拒答能力，以配对RGB为参照，并考察采样、输入呈现与推理等变量的影响。
candidates.contribution_zh: 揭示VLM在热成像人体活动理解中的失效模式：宽泛类别可识别，细粒度动作与时间线出错且产生物体幻觉，简单预处理与附加推理收益有限。

ai_review.reason: 在热成像人机交互场景中评测VLM的具身动作理解能力，属机器人感知与动作理解范畴。

candidates.title: NavBind: Diagnosing Instruction-Action Binding at Route Forks in Navigation VLAs
candidates.title_zh: NavBind：诊断导航VLA在路线分叉处的指令-动作绑定
candidates.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) navigation models translate visual observations and instructions into actions. Navigation success assesses whether an agent reaches the goal. However, reaching the goal successfully does not establish whether the model genuinely follows the instructions or relies on visual cues or navigation history. We introduce NavBind to diagnose instruction-action binding: whether changing the instruction influences the probabilistic distribution of the actions, with the navigation context fixed. We construct 3,252 route-fork contexts by recombining route-aligned instruction segments from R2R-CE and RxR-CE. Each context pairs full instructions that share the description of the route already traveled but specify different branches. Both are evaluated under the same agent state and navigation history. We compare generated local action sequences, the likelihoods of fixed reference action sequences under both instructions, and changes in visual attention and attribution. Across the evaluated models, higher reported navigation success does not imply that the model more faithfully follows the instructions.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出NavBind诊断基准，在固定导航上下文下改变指令，检验VLA动作分布是否随指令变化；构建3252个路线分叉场景，比较动作序列、似然与注意力归因。
candidates.contribution_zh: 揭示导航成功率不等于指令遵循，提供路线分叉式指令-动作绑定评测方法与证据。

ai_review.reason: 面向导航VLA的指令-动作绑定诊断，属具身智能与动作接地，应收录。

candidates.title: How Representational Priors Shape Generalization in World Action Models
candidates.title_zh: 表征先验如何塑造世界动作模型的泛化
candidates.abstract: World action models (WAMs) are shown to substantially diverge under generalization performance based on their generative backbones. We investigate this gap through the representational geometry that WAMs inherit from their backbones and how policy training reorganizes it. Our central hypothesis is that a useful representational prior would structure geometry that separates nuisance information from the in-distribution manifold in advance of training as a policy. We quantify this with nuisance orthogonality; orthogonality of the feature under visual variation outside the empirical in-distribution manifold. Across various image and video backbones, we show that a higher orthogonality from the representational prior is associated with stronger robustness to visual variations after WAM training, enabling policy generalization measurable prospectively for world models. In addition, analyzing the resulting robust WAMs reveals nuisance suppression; relative suppression of feature displacement caused by such variations and robust action generation of the policy. Together, these findings provide a geometric perspective on how the representational prior of the world model shapes the generalization performance of WAMs.
candidates.summary_zh: 论文研究世界动作模型因生成骨干不同而产生的泛化差异，提出用干扰正交性刻画表征先验，发现更高正交性预示更强视觉变化鲁棒性与策略泛化能力。
candidates.contribution_zh: 从表征几何角度解释世界模型先验如何影响世界动作模型的泛化，并提供可前瞻测量的鲁棒性指标。

candidates.title: SimPT: An Automated Simulation Framework for Intervention-Based VLA Post-Training
candidates.title_zh: SimPT：面向基于干预的VLA后训练的自动化仿真框架
candidates.abstract: Human-in-the-loop (HIL) post-training improves vision-language-action (VLA) policies through expert corrections, but costly human supervision and repeated real-robot evaluation limit algorithm exploration and development. We introduce SimPT (Simulation-based Post-Training), a simulation framework that automates intervention-based VLA post-training by integrating policy rollouts, corrective data collection, policy training, and standalone evaluation. To automatically determine intervention timing and recovery strategies, we develop an Agent-Compiled Progress Graph that tracks task progress using privileged simulator state and retains stable snapshots during policy execution. After a rollout fails, a CuRobo-based expert attempts recovery from these snapshots, starting at more advanced task stages and falling back to earlier ones as needed to generate corrective trajectories. We implement and compare four post-training methods, RECAP, HG-DAgger, DPO+SFT, and FlowPRO, across seven RoboTwin manipulation tasks. Relative to a fixed-interval snapshot baseline, the Progress Graph reduces recovery attempts by 75.0% and increases recovery success from 93.4% to 98.9%. Using SimPT, we develop RECAP-CF-LPF, a refinement of RECAP that combines cross-fitting and low-pass filtering of value predictions. This refinement increases the overall success rate from 76.50% to 79.36% in held-out simulation trials. In real-robot HIL post-training, it increases the success rate from 72% to 96% across 25 scenarios of an Ethernet cable-insertion task. These results demonstrate the utility of SimPT for exploring and developing VLA post-training algorithms.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出SimPT仿真框架，自动完成VLA策略的 rollout、干预纠错数据采集、训练与独立评估；用进度图自动确定干预时机与恢复策略，并在七个操作任务上比较四种后训练方法。
candidates.contribution_zh: 构建自动化干预式VLA后训练仿真框架，进度图减少75%恢复尝试并将恢复成功率提至98.9%，提出RECAP-CF-LPF提升仿真与真机成功率。

ai_review.reason: 面向VLA策略的仿真后训练框架，直接服务机器人操作与动作学习

candidates.title: Steering Black-Box Large Language Model Agents with Pitfall Anticipation World Model
candidates.title_zh: 用缺陷预判世界模型引导黑盒大语言模型智能体
candidates.abstract: Frontier black-box Large Language Model (LLM) agents are proficient at long-horizon reasoning and precise action generation. However, when it comes to a specific agentic task, they have no internalized knowledge of how that particular environment unfolds. A world model offers a natural remedy, providing the agent with environment specific knowledge by foreseeing how the environment will respond to the action it is about to take. Prior world models for LLM agents mainly predict next observations at each step, which is costly and often uninformative because individual observations provide limited task-relevant guidance and not every step requires call for foresight. This raises a key question: what a world model should predict and when should it be invoked for agentic tasks? Our pilot study suggests that world model guidance is most useful when it anticipates pitfalls within a bounded multi-step future. Motivated by this, we introduce Pitfall Anticipation World Model (PAWM), which selectively intervenes when a potential pitfall arises and predicts the impending failure to steer the agent away from it. PAWM is trained in two stages: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) on synthetic data labeled with agent pitfalls, followed by GRPO co-training with a black-box LLM to further optimize it in the target environment. PAWM improves Claude Sonnet 4.5 performance by 24.3% on ScienceWorld and 7.7% on WebArena-Lite, outperforming a range of baselines. These results demonstrate that PAWM provides an effective form of world model guidance for black-box LLM agents.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出缺陷预判世界模型PAWM，仅在预测到多步内有失败风险时介入，先在有缺陷标注的合成数据上微调，再与黑盒LLM用GRPO协同训练，在ScienceWorld与WebArena-Lite上提升表现。
candidates.contribution_zh: 以“何时调用、预测何物”重构智能体世界模型：选择性预判即将发生的失败并引导规避，替代逐步预测下一观测。

ai_review.reason: 面向文本LLM智能体的世界模型，实验仅ScienceWorld与WebArena网页任务，无机器人或物理具身成分。

candidates.title: Causal world models under physical parameter shifts
candidates.title_zh: 物理参数偏移下的因果世界模型
candidates.abstract: World models predict how embodied systems evolve under actions, but their accuracy can degrade when physical conditions move outside the training distribution. We study two components of causal modeling: which inputs a predictor may use, and how its mechanism computes their effects. In a synthetic benchmark with shortcut features, a frozen dependency mask derived from paired interventions reduces mean out-of-distribution (OOD) RMSE from 1.769 for a fully connected predictor to 0.697, close to the generator-oracle mask (0.694). For robot link-mass extrapolation in CausalWorld, with disjoint training and test mass ranges, we develop finger-local world models in which link masses enter inertia and dynamics-bias terms through explicit affine coefficients, actions act through either a learned torque network or the known PD controller, and learned residuals capture contact-related effects. Compared with a separately trained control whose mass inputs are fixed at training means, the known-PD model turns out-of-range masses into a consistent predictive gain: median time-averaged joint R2 over 150-step rollouts rises from 0.609 to 0.727, with improvement in all ten task-seed runs (exact two-sided sign test, p = 0.002). In a shared 100-step forecast, the learned-torque model is competitive with the strongest recurrent robotic world model (RWM) configuration (median joint R2 of 0.755 - 0.768 versus 0.752), whereas supplying out-of-range masses sharply degrades the MLP and recurrent predictors. These results indicate that how a physical parameter enters the dynamics mechanism determines whether its out-of-range value helps or harms prediction.

candidates.title: OccJEPA: Occlusion as Masking for Amodal Video Segmentation
candidates.title_zh: OccJEPA：以遮挡为掩码的非模态视频分割
candidates.abstract: Amodal video segmentation asks for the complete mask of an object in every frame, including the parts hidden behind other objects. The best current methods generate these masks with fine-tuned video diffusion models, which need many denoising steps and an extra depth network, and give a different answer for every sample. Self-supervised video world models of the JEPA family are trained on a closely related task: predicting the representation of masked space-time regions from the visible ones. We therefore treat occlusion as masking. The tokens that the object's visible mask does not cover are dropped, the pre-trained V-JEPA 2.1 predictor fills them in, and a light head decodes the observed and predicted features into amodal masks. The resulting model, OccJEPA (Occlusion-as-masking JEPA), is deterministic and 33.5x faster than the diffusion-based state of the art, and more accurate on SAIL-VOS, on TAO-Amodal, including a held-out test split (+4.00 AP50) and visible masks tracked by SAM2, and on Kubric. Controlled experiments trace the gain to the predictor's pre-trained weights rather than to its capacity, for world models from 87M to 1.85B parameters. Code is available at https://github.com/zgp110/occjepa.
candidates.summary_zh: 将遮挡视为掩码，利用预训练V-JEPA 2.1预测器补全被遮挡区域表征，并用轻量头解码观测与预测特征，生成每帧完整非模态掩码；方法确定性且较扩散基线快33.5倍。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出遮挡即掩码的非模态视频分割框架，复用V-JEPA预训练预测器补全遮挡表征，无需多步扩散与深度网络，在多个数据集上提升精度并显著加速。

provenance.source_comment: 20 pages (8-page main paper + supplementary material). Code: https://github.com/zgp110/occjepa

ai_review.reason: 面向通用视频非模态分割，未涉及机器人、动作或具身决策，不属物理智能核心范围。

candidates.title: Self-Improving Agents with World Model Predictive Paths
candidates.title_zh: 基于世界模型预测路径的自改进智能体
candidates.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly expected to interact with environments and improve their decisions during deployment. However, how anticipating future outcomes and drawing on accumulated interaction experience can jointly support decision-making remains underexplored. We propose a test-time framework, inspired by Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control, that combines multi-branch predictive analysis with experience-based adaptation. At each step, the agent proposes multiple candidate actions and imagines their outcomes with a world model, so that alternatives can be compared without being executed in the environment. Since language environments provide neither explicit dynamics nor costs, the predicted outcomes are evaluated for task progress and risk, and MPPI-style weights over the resulting costs guide the final decision. A dual-branch experience memory enables self-improvement: the planner branch refines candidate generation and action selection, while the world model branch improves next-observation prediction. Experiments on ALFWorld and ScienceWorld across three backbones demonstrate the strong overall performance of our method and the effectiveness of experience-guided predictive control. Our code will be made publicly available.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出一种测试时框架，结合多分支预测与经验记忆，用世界模型想象候选动作后果，并以MPPI式权重指导LLM智能体决策。
candidates.contribution_zh: 将MPPI式预测控制与双分支经验记忆结合，用于文本环境中的LLM智能体自改进决策。

ai_review.reason: 面向文本语言环境的LLM智能体规划，非机器人或物理智能，超出收录范围

candidates.title: Real2Sem2Real: 3D Semantic Augmentations for Robot Learning from a Single Human RGB Demonstration
candidates.title_zh: Real2Sem2Real：基于单个人类RGB演示的机器人学习三维语义增强
candidates.abstract: Human video scales easily and does not need robot hardware, but existing methods require depth sensing, overlay the robot onto 2D video, or generate data only for the demonstrated objects. We present Real2Sem2Real (R2Sem2R), a real-to-semantic-to-real pipeline that turns one monocular RGB video of a human demonstration into thousands of robot demonstrations across the semantic object instances of a category. R2Sem2R tracks the SE(3) pose of each object with DINOv3-distilled Gaussian splats, outperforming existing methods and FoundationPose with estimated metric depth. R2Sem2R then aligns digital cousins, each generated from one or a few photographs, to the demonstrated objects with a semantic alignment. This alignment matches whole objects and the functional regions of target objects, such as a coffee machine's tray. R2Sem2R maps the human hand to a feasible robot grasp that extends to the cousins. Robot demonstrations are generated either in IsaacSim, for photorealistic rendering, or MuJoCo, for contact physics, and R2Sem2R can generate over 2,000 episodes in about two hours. On two real robots and four tasks, we train a vision-language-action policy on data from one human video per task, and policies trained on our data match or exceed policies trained on teleoperation across diverse object instances. The project page is available at https://real2sem2real.github.io/.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出从单目人类演示视频到机器人示范数据的实到语义再实流水线，利用高斯泼溅跟踪物体位姿、语义对齐同类物体并映射抓取，经仿真生成数千条数据训练VLA策略。
candidates.contribution_zh: 仅用单个人类RGB视频即可跨同类物体生成大规模机器人示范，并在真实机器人多任务上匹配或超越遥操作数据训练的VLA策略。

provenance.source_comment: Matthew Strong and Ankush K. Dhawan contributed equally. Project page: https://real2sem2real.github.io/

ai_review.reason: 属机器人学习与VLA数据生成，直接服务物理智能，符合收录范围。

candidates.title: WorldStream: Streaming Interactive 3D Worlds with Hierarchical Planning and Persistent State
candidates.title_zh: WorldStream：具有分层规划与持久状态的流式交互三维世界
candidates.abstract: We present WorldStream, an open-ended 3D world model with three simultaneous capabilities: it extends playable terrain beyond any pre-specified map, acts on open-ended language in the running world, and restores visited places with their edits. A hierarchical planner over a typed decision model emits structured decision state: Macro fixes settlement, ecology, transport, and hydrological structure across a group of tiles; Micro specializes that contract into tile semantics under measured terrain and accepted neighbor commitments. Deterministic local code compiles accepted plans into terrain, roads, settlements, vegetation, and entities. Streaming separates their reach: plans run ahead along the predicted corridor, compilation only where movement will soon need it, geometry behind the user released. One world record retains plans, seeds, object identities and mutable state, boundary commitments, and edits by attribute, revised as the user advances and edits; returning tiles recompile from it. The same record grounds interaction: the model acts on existing entities, including stateful NPCs that update as they act, edits the present region, or attaches intent to unplanned regions. Together they yield a world expanding under bounded budgets, connected across independently planned tiles, and interactive.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出流式交互三维世界模型：分层规划器产出结构化决策，在预算内编译地形、道路、聚落与实体；持久世界记录保存计划、种子、编辑与边界承诺，支持回访重建和开放语言交互。
candidates.contribution_zh: 以宏/微分层规划加确定性编译与流式生成，配合持久状态记录，实现可扩展、可编辑、可交互的三维世界。

candidates.title: Second Thoughts: Exploring and Planning through Comparative Imagination in World Models
candidates.title_zh: Second Thoughts：在世界模型中通过比较想象进行探索与规划
candidates.abstract: World models let agents compare imagined outcomes before acting, but an agent must still decide which alternatives to explore and when a proposed plan should replace its learned policy. We introduce SDI (Sibling Disagreement in Imagination), which connects these decisions through a shared actor-based reference. SDI compares action sequences imagined from the same model state, using repeated rollouts of the actor's own sequence to measure variation under fixed behavior. This reference scales both the spread across candidate returns, which provides an exploration signal, and a proposed plan's predicted advantage, which governs action acceptance. The agent executes a planned action when its advantage exceeds the reference variability by a fixed factor; otherwise, it follows the actor. SDI reuses the base agent's world model, actor, and critic without requiring an additional disagreement ensemble. Exploration and planning guide training data collection, while evaluation uses the learned actor alone. Across Meta-World, Adroit, and DM-Control, SDI achieves a higher observed task-average score than every compared baseline in each suite and matches or exceeds the strongest baseline's performance on 15 of 18 tasks. Component ablations and robustness analyses further examine the roles of exploration, planning exposure, and action acceptance. Paired evaluations from identical simulator states show that the gate improves both recovery from actor failures and preservation of successful behavior relative to ungated planning, while substantially reducing return degradation. Together, these results support comparing imagined alternatives against a shared actor reference as a unified approach to exploring and planning with world models.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出SDI：用世界模型对同一状态的动作序列重复想象，以actor自身序列变化为共享参考，统一探索信号与计划接受门控；在Meta-World、Adroit、DM-Control上提升表现并减少规划退化。
candidates.contribution_zh: 无需额外分歧集成，复用世界模型、actor和critic，将想象比较用于探索与规划门控，并在多个机器人控制基准验证。

ai_review.reason: 面向世界模型中的想象规划与探索，并在机器人控制基准验证，符合收录范围。

candidates.title: Understanding the Inner Workings of a State-Space Foundation Model for Limit Order Books
candidates.title_zh: 理解面向限价订单簿的状态空间基础模型内部机制
candidates.abstract: Autoregressive foundation models offer state-of-the-art capabilities to simulate the market by generating the message flow of limit order books (LOBs). Yet, without understanding their inner workings, research directions are hard to narrow and practical use in real-world trading environments remains uncertain. This study therefore asks what these models actually learn about market microstructure. We find that, similarly to games where sequence models build an internal representation of the board, an 8.2M-parameter Mamba-3 state-space model trained autoregressively on the tokenized message stream of eight large-cap US equities learns an internal representation of the market and its dynamics. In particular, order-flow imbalance, a central driver of short-horizon price moves, is decodable at $R^2 \approx 0.59$, far above controls and baselines. This representation extends to unseen stocks, suggesting that these models learn general representations rather than ticker-specific patterns. The model also generalizes across metrics beyond order-flow imbalance: results hold across traded volume and volatility. Additionally, the representation is causally steerable: pushing the state along a feature's axis shifts the model's next-message beliefs as that feature implies, monotonically in dose, consistent with the emergence of a world model.
candidates.summary_zh: 研究自回归 Mamba-3 状态空间模型在美股订单流数据上的内部表示，发现订单流不平衡等微观结构特征可线性解码、跨股票泛化且可因果操控。
candidates.contribution_zh: 揭示订单簿序列模型内部形成可解码、可泛化、可操控的市场动力学表示。
